Checklist Item: Semantic-to-div ratio above threshold; pages with >70% generic containers (div/span) flagged
Comments: Generic containers (div/span) account for ~36% of HTML element usage in JS blocks (25 div/span vs 45 semantic elements). Well below the 70% flagging threshold.

Checklist Item: Correct heading hierarchy maintained
Comments: Blocks use querySelector to find and preserve authored heading elements (h1-h6) from content. Programmatic heading creation uses appropriate levels (h2 in resume-application, h3 in accordion, accordion-section, campaign-lists, campaign-ctas, contact-tile-individual). Heading hierarchy is generally maintained and respected from authored content.

Checklist Item: Single h1 per page where applicable
Comments: No block programmatically creates h1 elements. Blocks query and preserve authored headings. campaign-ctas explicitly comments 'rendered as an h3, a sensible module-title level under a page's own h1/h2', showing awareness of h1 ownership. Single h1 is enforced at the content authoring level.

Checklist Item: DOM source order matches visual tab order; no positive tabindex values; CSS order/flex-direction does not contradict DOM sequence
Comments: No positive tabindex values found; header uses roving tabindex (0/-1) correctly per ARIA tabs pattern. However, 5 blocks use flex-direction reverse (row-reverse in text-with-image, campaign-ctas; column-reverse in hero-banner-carousel x2, midpage-banner), which can create a visual/tab-order mismatch for keyboard users.

Checklist Item: Page content hierarchy intact: headings and body text present in raw HTML source; critical content not injected solely via JavaScript; no content exclusively hidden via inline style or JS-only class toggling
Comments: AEM EDS architecture serves pre-rendered HTML from CDN; JS decorates existing DOM rather than injecting critical content. innerHTML usages are limited to UI decoration elements (play buttons, icons with alt=""). Fragment block loads server-rendered HTML via fetch. Content headings and body text are present in raw HTML source from the delivery tier.

Checklist Item: Avoid excessive DOM depth
Comments: EDS blocks reuse existing content columns from authored HTML tables, minimising re-nesting. Programmatic DOM construction wraps existing elements rather than creating deep nesting chains. Typical block depth is 4-6 levels (block > row > col > content), which is acceptable.

Checklist Item: Radio/checkbox groups wrapped in fieldset with legend; forms with 3+ related inputs have grouping
Comments: site-selector creates radio inputs for language selection wrapped in a <ul> without a <fieldset>/<legend>, missing proper grouping. product-details-card uses ARIA role='radiogroup'/'radio' on custom chips without native fieldset/legend. No fieldset or legend elements found anywhere in blocks JS.

Checklist Item: All inputs have associated labels
Comments: All inputs have accessible labels. Search inputs (blocks/search, site-selector) use aria-label with the placeholder text value. Radio inputs in site-selector use proper label[for]/id pairing (radioLabel.htmlFor = optionId, radio.id = optionId). No unlabelled inputs found.

Checklist Item: Placeholder not used as label
Comments: Search inputs in blocks/search and site-selector set both placeholder and aria-label with the same value, ensuring placeholder is supplementary not the sole label. No inputs rely solely on placeholder text for labelling.

Checklist Item: Error messages programmatically associated with inputs via aria-describedby or aria-errormessage; error containers use role='alert' or aria-live='assertive'; error text is non-empty and >10 characters
Comments: Partial: sbg-dividend-calculator sets aria-invalid on invalid inputs but does not programmatically associate error messages via aria-describedby or aria-errormessage. share-price-interactive-chart uses role='alert' for error messages (good for live announcements) but messages are not linked to specific inputs. No aria-errormessage usage found anywhere.

Checklist Item: Avoid inline styles
Comments: 28 inline style usages found. Some are justified (CSS custom properties for dynamic icon src, embed aspect ratio, runtime height capture). However some are avoidable: embed.js uses style.cssText for layout, hero-banner-no-carousel uses style.display, tab-section and tabs-text-only use style.order, ctas-teaser uses style.minHeight for equalization. These could be managed via CSS classes.

Checklist Item: Accessible names for interactive elements
Comments: All interactive elements have accessible names. 54 aria-label attributes across 43 created buttons. Pattern is consistent: close buttons get aria-label ('Close alert', localised via placeholders), carousel navigation buttons get i18n-aware labels with English fallbacks ('Previous slide', 'Next slide', 'Go to slide {{index}}'), icon-only buttons use aria-label, text-containing buttons use textContent.

Checklist Item: Images with role='presentation' or aria-hidden='true' have empty alt; standalone without adjacent text and without alt flagged; hero/banner images verified to have non-empty alt >10 chars; in decorative containers verified to have empty alt or role='presentation'
Comments: Strong alt text pattern throughout. Decorative icons use aria-hidden='true'. Play button imgs have alt='' (parent button has aria-label). Programmatic img elements: buttons-list-carousel derives alt from link.title||textContent; logo sets alt='' for decorative brand marks (with explicit comment); icons block reads alt from authored imageAlt field with fallback to '' . All patterns are correct.

Checklist Item: Alt text is not a filename or path; not generic (image/photo/icon/picture/graphic/banner/logo without qualifier); between 5-125 characters; does not duplicate adjacent text content; does not begin with 'image of'/'picture of'/'photo of'; alt on linked images describes destination
Comments: No hardcoded filename paths or generic alt text found in code. All programmatic alt values are either empty string (decorative) or derived from authored content (link.title, link.textContent, imageAlt field). Alt text quality for content images is an authoring-time responsibility; the code correctly passes through or derives meaningful values.

Checklist Item: Tables use thead and tbody
Comments: The table block reads authored HTML tables from the CMS RTE. The code checks for <th> elements and supports a 'header row' toggle but does not programmatically wrap rows into <thead>/<tbody> elements. thead/tbody structure is entirely dependent on the RTE output, and no enforcement or normalisation is applied in the block's decorate function.

Checklist Item: Table headers use th
Comments: table.js explicitly supports <th> elements from the RTE 'header row' toggle and checks for them via table.querySelector('th'). A 'header-row' CSS class is applied as fallback when no <th> elements exist (for zero-effort authoring). The code correctly handles both real <th> and fallback scenarios. th usage depends on authors using the RTE header row property.

Checklist Item: Lists use ul or ol correctly
Comments: Lists are semantically correct throughout. ul is used for unordered groupings (cards, social-media-links, dropdown options, contact tiles, ctas-teaser etc.). ol is correctly used for ordered sequences: breadcrumb (breadcrumbs are ordered) and timeline (ordered chronological steps). No lists misuse - proper ul/ol/li nesting.

Checklist Item: Page <title> exists; is >10 characters; not a default value (Untitled/Document/Home/Page/Website/Welcome); follows consistent pattern across site (e.g. 'Page - Site' or 'Page | Site' separator detected)
Comments: Page <title> is managed via AEM EDS metadata authoring (not hardcoded in code). head.html does not define a static title; titles are set per-page by authors in the metadata sheet. No default/fallback titles are set in scripts. The code does not override document.title. Title quality and pattern consistency are an authoring governance concern.

Checklist Item: Meta viewport configured correctly
Comments: Meta viewport is correctly configured in head.html: <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"/>. Uses standard width=device-width and initial-scale=1. No user-scalable=no or maximum-scale restriction that would block zoom.

Checklist Item: No duplicate IDs
Comments: All blocks with dynamic IDs use incrementing counter-based nextId(prefix) functions generating unique IDs like 'accordion-header-1', 'accordion-header-2', etc. Pattern is consistent across accordion, dropdown, tab-section, tabs-text-only, related-links, sbg-dividend-calculator. nextPopoverId utility used for popover IDs. No hardcoded duplicate IDs found.

Checklist Item: No invalid HTML nesting
Comments: No invalid HTML nesting patterns found in code. No button-inside-anchor or anchor-inside-button patterns. Buttons and anchors are separate elements. The EDS pattern of styled anchor tags (with .button class) for CTAs avoids the common invalid button-inside-link antipattern. DOM construction follows proper parent-child nesting rules.

Checklist Item: HTML validates without errors
Comments: Code review shows no invalid nesting, correct semantic elements, proper attribute usage, unique IDs, and valid aria attributes. Full W3C HTML validation of rendered pages requires a browser audit. From static code analysis: correct heading hierarchy, no known invalid nesting patterns, no duplicate IDs, no missing required attributes detected.
Evidence: blocks/ (all JS files reviewed in prior items)

Checklist Item: ARIA roles do not duplicate native semantics
Comments: ARIA roles are used correctly and purposefully. role='listbox'/'option' on ul/li elements are correct for a custom select/combobox widget (override native list semantics intentionally). role='radio' on button chips in product-details-card is an acceptable custom widget pattern. role='search' on form is an acceptable landmark specialization. tablist/tab/tabpanel on divs follows correct ARIA tab pattern. No redundant roles (e.g., role='button' on button).

Checklist Item: Avoid misuse of ARIA roles
Comments: All ARIA roles are used correctly for their intended purpose: listbox/option for custom combobox, radiogroup/radio for custom chip selector, search on form/div landmarks, tablist/tab/tabpanel for tab widgets, group+aria-roledescription='slide' for carousel slides (correct per ARIA carousel pattern), alert for error messages, status for snackbar notifications, tooltip for product details.

Checklist Item: ARIA used only when necessary
Comments: ARIA is used only where necessary. Custom widgets (dropdown/combobox, tabs, carousel, radio chip selector) require ARIA because native HTML has no equivalent. Live regions (aria-live='polite' for dividend calculator results, share price updates, snackbar) are appropriate. aria-hidden='true' on decorative icons is correct. aria-label on icon-only buttons is necessary. No superfluous ARIA found.

Checklist Item: Meta tags do not block zoom
Comments: Viewport meta in head.html is: content='width=device-width, initial-scale=1'. No user-scalable=no, no maximum-scale, no minimum-scale restrictions. Users can freely zoom the page.

Checklist Item: No broken links (run broken-link-checker or linkinator CLI against local build or source HTML)
Comments: Static code audit cannot verify broken links - this requires a browser/runtime check against a live or staging URL. No hardcoded absolute links found in block JS; all links are authored content passed through from CMS. The fragment block fetches content from relative URLs. Recommend running linkinator or broken-link-checker against the deployed site as part of browser audit.

Checklist Item: CSS variables used for all colors
Comments: Most colors correctly use CSS custom properties (var(--color-name)). However hardcoded colors found: sbg-dividend-calculator.css uses #fff instead of var(--white-color); hero-banner-no-carousel.css, logos-with-overlay.css, midpage-banner-full-width.css, modal.css use hardcoded rgb() for semi-transparent overlays. vertical-scroller-tokens.css defines a token with rgb(255 255 255 / 60%) as the value (acceptable for token definition). header.css uses CSS relative color syntax rgb(from var(--white-color) r g b / 20%) which is acceptable.

Checklist Item: CSS variables used for spacing scale
Comments: A spacing token system exists in styles.css (--spacing-general-section-padding-lr/tb, --spacing-general-page-gap-xs/base/sm/md/lg, --spacing-general-gap). However 24 block CSS files use hardcoded rem/px values for padding and margin instead of referencing spacing tokens. Examples: cards.css uses margin:16px, ctas.css uses padding:2.188rem 3.125rem. Spacing tokens are under-utilised across the block library.

Checklist Item: CSS variables used for typography scale
Comments: A comprehensive typography token system exists in styles.css (--font-size-body-s/xs/button/heading-s/main/page/module-title/module-sub-title/entrance/body-text/notes/h5/number, --font-weight-regular/medium/bold, --line-height-tight/body-loose). However many blocks use hardcoded rem values: dropdown.css, app-promo-banner.css, product-details-card.css, text-with-image.css, content-display-features.css, contact-tile.css and others bypass the token system.

Checklist Item: No hardcoded hex/rgb color values
Comments: 26 hardcoded hex/rgb color values found across blocks. Key violations: sbg-dividend-calculator.css uses #fff instead of var(--white-color); cards.css uses #dadada for border; hero-banner-carousel.css and midpage-banner-full-width.css hardcode #00164e (brand dark blue) in gradients; multiple blocks use hardcoded rgb() for semi-transparent overlays and box shadows. These should use CSS variables.

Checklist Item: No hardcoded pixel spacing where tokens exist
Comments: 24 instances of hardcoded pixel/rem spacing values found in block CSS where spacing tokens (--spacing-general-*) exist. Examples: cards.css uses margin:16px instead of a token, ctas.css uses padding:2.188rem 3.125rem, campaign-lists.css, social-share.css, cta-with-country-selector.css etc. The global spacing token system in styles.css is underutilised by the block library.

Checklist Item: Consistent naming conventions
Comments: Consistent BEM-like naming convention throughout. Block directories use kebab-case (accordion, hero-banner-carousel, sbg-dividend-calculator). CSS classes follow block-name-element pattern: dropdown-trigger, dropdown-trigger-label, dropdown-trigger-icon, campaign-lists-item, campaign-lists-item-content, social-media-links-items, social-media-links-icon etc. JS function names use camelCase. CSS custom properties use --block-name-property kebab-case.

Checklist Item: Class names do not contain hex values or color names as identifiers; no purely positional names (left1/col2); BEM or project naming convention pattern enforced
Comments: No purely positional names (col1/row2) found. No hex values in class names. However color names are used as variant identifiers: hero-banner-carousel variants are named 'blue-small', 'blue-curve', 'blue-video' and used extensively in CSS. These are authored block variant names from the content model - while representing a design vocabulary, naming variants after colors couples naming to presentation. No BEM violations otherwise; block-name-element pattern is consistently followed.

Checklist Item: CSS selectors for same component co-located in same file; no duplicate selectors scattered across files; related rules grouped by component
Comments: AEM EDS architecture enforces CSS co-location by design. Each block has its own directory (blocks/block-name/) containing block-name.js and block-name.css. All CSS rules for a component live in that component's CSS file. vertical-scroller further separates design tokens into vertical-scroller-tokens.css within the same directory - a good modular pattern. No cross-block selector scattering found.

Checklist Item: Layout containers use display:flex or display:grid; no float:left/right for multi-column layouts; no display:table for non-tabular content; absolute positioning in <5% of layout containers
Comments: No float:left/right for multi-column layouts found. No display:table for non-tabular content. 317 flex/grid declarations show modern layout approach. However, 69 position:absolute instances found, representing ~18% of layout declarations vs the <5% guideline. Many are for overlay effects, icons, and decorative elements which may be appropriate, but the count warrants review.
Evidence: blocks/ (317 flex/grid, 69 position:absolute across all block CSS files)

Checklist Item: min-width media queries outnumber max-width queries; base styles (outside media queries) target mobile viewport dimensions
Comments: Mobile-first approach confirmed. All 357 media queries use modern CSS range syntax (width >= breakpoint), the equivalent of min-width queries. Examples: @media (width >= 768px), @media (width >= 1024px). No max-width queries found. Base styles outside media queries target mobile dimensions. This is correct mobile-first pattern.

Checklist Item: Standard breakpoints only
Comments: Only two breakpoints used across all 357 media queries: 768px (234 uses) and 1024px (113 uses). No non-standard or one-off breakpoints found in media queries. These match the standard tablet (768px) and desktop (1024px) breakpoints defined for this project.
Evidence: blocks/ (all CSS files - grep of @media breakpoints)

Checklist Item: Responsive images by default
Comments: Responsive images implemented throughout. 185 references to srcset/picture/optimizeResponsivePicture/createOptimizedPicture. AEM's createOptimizedPicture generates <picture> elements with srcset for multiple breakpoints. A custom optimizeResponsivePicture utility adds smart-crop support for Dynamic Media. Blocks using images (hero banners, carousels, product-details-card, text-with-image, campaign-lists, vertical-scroller) all use responsive picture elements.

Checklist Item: Avoid z-index escalation
Comments: Z-index values are well-controlled with no escalation wars. Range: -1 (background elements) to 100 (social-share snackbar notification). Modal uses z-index:98. Most values are 1-3 for local stacking contexts. search.css documents its z-index:3 reasoning in a comment. No arbitrary large values (999, 9999) found. Values are purposeful and proportional.

Checklist Item: Avoid expensive box-shadows
Comments: Box shadows are minimal and contained. Most use var(--box-shadow) CSS token. Hardcoded shadows have small blur radii (0.25-0.75rem) and low opacity (10-25%). No large spread values, no inset shadows stacked multiple layers, no excessively large blur radii (>1rem). Shadow usage is restrained to dropdowns, modals, header scroll state, and card hover effects.

Checklist Item: Avoid heavy CSS filters
Comments: No CSS filter properties found in any block or style CSS files. Icon masking uses mask-image (CSS masking, not filter) which is GPU-composited and performant. No blur, brightness, contrast, drop-shadow or other CSS filter effects used.

Checklist Item: No infinite CSS animations on non-loading elements; animation duration under 1s; total animation count per page within threshold
Comments: Only 2 infinite animations found, both on loading spinners (appropriate): midpage-banner-full-width video loader spin at 0.8s, and page loader-spin at 1s. A 3s animation-duration is set (likely for reduced-motion or skeleton). No infinite animations on non-loading content elements. Animation counts are minimal per page.

Checklist Item: All CSS properties/values supported in target browsers (checked against caniuse compatibility data); no unprefixed experimental features without fallbacks
Comments: Most CSS is well-supported. Concerns: (1) -webkit-line-clamp with display:-webkit-box used in hero-banner-no-carousel (required for text truncation, acceptable). (2) :has() selector used in numbers.css and specialised-share-price-historical.css - good Chrome/Safari support but Firefox 121+ only; no fallback provided. (3) CSS nesting (&:has()) in numbers.css requires modern browsers. (4) rgb(from var(--white-color)) CSS relative color in header.css has limited browser support. (5) No explicit browser target or browserslist config found.

Checklist Item: Avoid vendor prefixes unless required
Comments: Vendor prefixes are used only where required. -webkit-line-clamp/-webkit-box/-webkit-box-orient combination is the standard multi-line text truncation technique (still requires these webkit prefixes). ::-webkit-scrollbar is needed for custom scrollbar styling in Chromium-based browsers. No unnecessary vendor prefixes found (no -webkit- on transitions, transforms, flexbox, grid, or other properties that no longer require prefixing).

Checklist Item: No duplicated CSS rules
Comments: CSS co-location per block (one CSS file per block) significantly limits duplicate rule risk. Common property names (color, background, border) appear across different block CSS files as expected and acceptable. Within-file duplicate rules: the media query structure (base + 768px + 1024px) means property overrides are intentional responsive progressions, not duplicates. No CSS linting tool is configured (no stylelint CSS rule deduplication); a static analysis pass is recommended.
Evidence: blocks/ (all CSS files co-located per block)

Checklist Item: No unused CSS selectors
Comments: Static code analysis cannot definitively identify unused CSS selectors without a live rendered DOM. However, the EDS block architecture greatly reduces risk: each block's CSS is only loaded when that block is on the page. Block CSS files use block-name-scoped selectors (e.g. .hero-banner-carousel-*) that directly correspond to elements created in the block's JS. No global utility CSS classes or shared stylesheets detected beyond styles.css. Run PurgeCSS or browser DevTools coverage for definitive verification.

Checklist Item: Consistent property ordering
Comments: Stylelint is configured with stylelint-config-standard, which does not enforce CSS property ordering. No stylelint-order plugin or property-sort-order config found. A quick visual review of multiple block CSS files shows no consistent ordering convention (properties are not alphabetical, not grouped by box-model/typography/visual). Property ordering consistency is not enforced by tooling.

Checklist Item: No blocking scripts in head
Comments: No blocking scripts in head. Both scripts in head.html use type='module' which is deferred/non-blocking by default: <script nonce='aem' src='/scripts/aem.js' type='module'></script> and <script nonce='aem' src='/scripts/scripts.js' type='module'></script>. Module scripts are deferred automatically. No render-blocking <script> without async/defer found.

Checklist Item: Use async or defer appropriately
Comments: type='module' scripts are deferred by default (equivalent to defer attribute). Block JS files are dynamically imported via import() only when the block is observed in the viewport (lazy loading via AEM's loadSection/loadSections with IntersectionObserver pattern). No scripts use async incorrectly for DOM-dependent code. The architecture correctly separates eager (aem.js, scripts.js as modules) from lazy (block JS loaded on demand).

Checklist Item: Third-party scripts lazy loaded
Comments: Third-party scripts are loaded lazily. Google Maps API (maps.googleapis.com) is loaded on-demand with async and defer attributes, only when the address-with-map block is used. Embed block's loadScript is triggered only when the embed block renders. No third-party scripts are loaded eagerly in head.html. The AEM EDS pattern of loading blocks dynamically ensures third-party dependencies are never loaded until needed.

Checklist Item: No JS files loaded on pages where their exports are unused; code-split bundles match route usage
Comments: AEM EDS architecture inherently provides per-block code splitting. Each block's JS is dynamically imported only when that block exists on the page (loadBlock in aem.js uses dynamic import()). Block JS files are never loaded on pages where the block is absent. No bundling step - each block is its own module loaded on demand. This is the EDS core performance principle.

Checklist Item: No marketing tags in head
Comments: head.html contains no marketing tags. Only: CSP meta http-equiv, viewport meta, font preloads (BentonSansProBold.woff2, BentonSansProRegular.woff2), and two type='module' script tags. No GTM, Google Analytics, Adobe Analytics, Tealium, or other marketing/tracking scripts in the head.

Checklist Item: User-facing strings in component render/template functions reference i18n keys or constants; hardcoded display strings >3 words flagged
Comments: Strong i18n implementation. 131 references to fetchPlaceholders/placeholders across blocks. Pattern: placeholders loaded via fetchPlaceholders(), used with English fallbacks e.g. placeholders.closeAlert || 'Close alert', placeholders.close || 'Close'. Some short hardcoded fallbacks exist ('Play video', 'Previous slide', 'Next slide') where i18n has not yet been applied but are brief utility labels. No long hardcoded user-facing display strings found.

Checklist Item: No binaries stored in repository
Comments: Binary/vendor files committed to repo: (1) fonts/ directory contains 6 font files (BentonSansProBold/Medium/Regular in both .woff and .woff2) - acceptable for brand fonts. (2) scripts/utils/plyr/plyr.min.js - vendor video player binary committed to repo instead of using npm dependency. (3) scripts/dompurify.min.js - security library committed to repo. These vendor JS files should be managed as npm dependencies rather than committed binaries to enable version tracking and security updates.

Checklist Item: Error messages follow consistent pattern (checked via regex); no raw string throws; error constants or error classes used
Comments: Error messages follow consistent patterns: (1) throw new Error('descriptive message') for operational errors - API failures include status codes. (2) console.warn('block-name: message') for non-fatal warnings. (3) console.error('block-name: description', error) for caught errors. No raw string throws or custom Error classes. Namespace prefix pattern (block-name:) makes console messages easily identifiable. Consistent across all blocks and utilities.

Checklist Item: Avoid tight DOM coupling
Comments: AEM EDS requires positional block.children destructuring by design - each block's rows are defined by the content model (component-models.json). Destructuring pattern `const [row1, row2, ...items] = block.children` is idiomatic EDS and not pathological tight coupling. No cross-block DOM access detected. Blocks only access their own block element's children. No document.querySelector() for elements outside the block scope.

Checklist Item: Avoid forced synchronous layouts
Comments: Layout reads are generally batched before writes. ctas-teaser reads all offsetHeights first (Math.max spread), then writes all minHeights - correct batch pattern. header.js uses void list.offsetWidth deliberately to force CSS transition (intentional, one-time). BoundingClientRect calls in modal, timeline, tooltip, header are in event handlers (user-triggered) not in render loops. hero-banner-no-carousel reads offsetHeight once in a resize observer. No read-in-loop-then-write patterns detected.

Checklist Item: All setTimeout/setInterval calls have corresponding clear calls; timer count per file within threshold (max 3); no timers <100ms
Comments: All setTimeout calls have corresponding clearTimeout: dropdown typeahead (500ms), social-share snackbar (3000ms), modal fallback timer, header resize debounce. No setInterval found. modal.js uses setTimeout(0) for scroll reset (acceptable deferred DOM op). scripts.js uses 3000ms for delayed.js lazy load. ACCORDION_TRANSITION_MS references CSS transition duration. No timers < 100ms. All files have ≤3 timers. Pattern is clean.

Checklist Item: setInterval for DOM/state checks flagged (suggest MutationObserver/IntersectionObserver/EventListener); polling intervals <1s flagged
Comments: No setInterval calls found anywhere in the codebase. DOM observation uses IntersectionObserver (for lazy loading blocks and section reveals), MutationObserver (in editor-support.js for DOM changes), and ResizeObserver (in header and hero blocks). Event listeners used for state changes. Correct modern observer APIs are used throughout instead of polling.

Checklist Item: Prefer native browser APIs
Comments: Native browser APIs used throughout. No jQuery or DOM utility libraries. Animations use CSS transitions/transforms. DOM manipulation uses native createElement, appendChild, querySelector, classList. Fetch API used for data loading. IntersectionObserver, ResizeObserver, MutationObserver for DOM observation. Native <dialog> element used in modal block. requestAnimationFrame used in modal.js. History API for navigation. Only one third-party UI lib: plyr.min.js for video player (acceptable for complex media control).

Checklist Item: Modern ES6+ syntax used
Comments: Modern ES6+ syntax used consistently throughout: const/let (no var), arrow functions, async/await, destructuring assignment, template literals, spread operator, optional chaining (?.), nullish coalescing (??), dynamic import(), ES modules (import/export), Map/Set, for...of loops, Array methods (map/filter/reduce/find). No legacy patterns found. ESLint enforces standards via .eslintrc.js.

Checklist Item: Avoid memory leaks
Comments: Strong memory leak prevention: (1) Event listeners cleaned up in modal.js (removeEventListener for transitionend, keydown, click), header.js (keydown, focusout, transitionend). (2) Observers disconnected: IntersectionObserver.disconnect() in embed.js and scripts.js, ResizeObserver.disconnect() in video.js, hero-banner-no-carousel checks isConnected before continuing. (3) AbortController used in scripts.js for fetch cancellation. (4) video.js exposes destroy() method that disconnects ResizeObserver.

Checklist Item: Event listeners cleaned up properly
Comments: Event listeners are cleaned up appropriately. Transient listeners (transitionend, escape keydown) are removed immediately after first use via removeEventListener inside the handler. Modal cleans up document-level keydown and click listeners on close. Header cleans up window keydown and nav focusout on menu close. AbortController cleans up event listeners tied to fetch requests. Block-scoped listeners (click, scroll, resize) are on the block element itself and are GC'd with the element.

Checklist Item: Async logic uses async/await
Comments: async/await used consistently throughout for all asynchronous operations: fetch calls, dynamic import(), loadBlock/loadSection/loadCSS, fetchPlaceholders, Google Maps API loading. No raw .then()/.catch() chains for new code - .then() only seen where chaining is appropriate (e.g. window.googleMapsAPILoading = loadScript(...).then(...)). All block decorate functions that perform async work are declared async. Consistent pattern across all blocks and utilities.
Evidence: scripts/aem.js, scripts/utils/map.js:48-50, blocks/ (async decorate functions throughout)

Checklist Item: Promises handled correctly
Comments: Majority of async code uses async/await with try/catch. Promise.all used in accordion-section, modal, site-selector, breadcrumb. A few .then() chains (hero-banner-no-carousel, midpage-banner, midpage-banner-full-width) lack explicit .catch() but are non-critical placeholder fetches. Overall promise handling is solid.

Checklist Item: State changes occur through defined setters/reducers/actions; no direct state object property mutations outside state management layer
Comments: Project uses vanilla JS EDS architecture with no centralized state management layer — no Redux/Zustand/MobX. Each block manages its own local state through closure variables and DOM attributes (data-*, classList, aria-*). No shared mutable state objects are mutated across modules. State changes are encapsulated within block functions.
Evidence: blocks/ (all block files use closure-scoped local variables)

Checklist Item: No mutation of shared state
Comments: No exported mutable shared state found. Module-level `let` variables (sequence counters, cached promise singletons like sharePricePromise, plyrPromise) are module-internal and not exported. Each block scopes its state within its decorate() function or module. No global state objects are mutated across modules.

Checklist Item: No side effects in pure functions
Comments: Utility/helper functions in scripts/utils/ are pure: pad(), startOfDay(), isSameDay(), addDays(), toFeedDate(), parseSharePriceResponse(), clampDate(), inRange() are all pure (no side effects, return computed values). DOM-manipulating functions (block decorators) are clearly impure by design and not labelled as pure. Good separation between pure utilities and effectful block functions.

Checklist Item: Consistent return types
Comments: Return types are inconsistent across utilities. Some functions return null (svg.js, embed.js, share-price.js) while others return undefined (smart-crop.js findImageLink), false (sb-decorators.js, date-picker.js), or bare return; (no value) for error/empty cases. No TypeScript or JSDoc @returns annotations to enforce consistency. Not critical but inconsistent.

Checklist Item: Charset meta tag (<meta charset="UTF-8">) declared in <head> before any content-producing elements; charset declaration appears within first 1024 bytes of document
Comments: No <meta charset="UTF-8"> found in head.html or any HTML files. AEM EDS may inject charset at the CDN/platform layer before serving the HTML. head.html is a fragment appended to the <head> by aem.js - the charset should appear in the base document template. Since head.html is the only authored head content and it has no charset declaration, this cannot be verified from source alone. Recommend confirming charset is delivered by AEM platform in rendered HTML.
Evidence: head.html - no charset meta tag found. AEM EDS platform may inject it automatically at the document layer.

Checklist Item: Language attribute (lang) on <html> element is a valid BCP 47 tag matching page content language; lang attribute not empty or set to 'undefined'
Comments: scripts/scripts.js:232 hardcodes document.documentElement.lang = 'en' for all pages/locales. 'en' is a valid BCP 47 tag, but the site has multi-locale support (redirectRootToLocale in sb-decorators.js, /en/ paths). If other locales exist (e.g. /af/, /zu/ for South African languages), lang attribute will always be 'en' incorrectly. sb-decorators.js getLang() reads document.documentElement.lang with 'en' fallback (line 159). Lang should be derived from the URL locale path.

Checklist Item: Direction attribute (dir) specified on <html> or relevant container elements for RTL language pages; value is 'ltr' or 'rtl' matching content language direction
Comments: No dir attribute set - site is English-only (LTR direction). No RTL languages are implemented. The 'direction' references found are carousel navigation (prev/next), not text direction. Since the site is English-only (lang='en'), LTR is the default browser behavior and no explicit dir attribute is required. If Arabic/Hebrew etc. are added in future, dir='rtl' will need to be implemented.
Evidence: Site is English-only per scripts/scripts.js:232 (lang='en'). No RTL language support detected.

Checklist Item: Content elements have explicit width and height HTML attributes or CSS aspect-ratio set to reserve layout space and prevent CLS
Comments: createOptimizedPicture() in aem.js does NOT set width/height HTML attributes on the generated img element (unlike standard AEM EDS boilerplate). This can cause CLS as browsers don't know image dimensions before loading. Mitigating factor: many blocks use CSS aspect-ratio on image containers (cards.css:25 4/3, vertical-scroller.css:245 16/9, product-details-card.css:12 16/9, embed.css:20 16/9 etc.) which prevents layout shift. However not all blocks have aspect-ratio set, and the HTML-level width/height is absent.
Evidence: scripts/aem.js createOptimizedPicture() - no img.width/height set. blocks/cards/cards.css:25, blocks/embed/embed.css:20 (aspect-ratio as workaround)
